summaryBox.title: Zero-Order Integrated Kinetics
summaryBox.takeaway: [A]_t = [A]_0 - kt. Rate is constant (slope = 0 on Rate vs [A]). [A]_t vs t is linear with slope = -k.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ZERO-ORDER INTEGRATED KINETICS
                       
   Differential Rate Law:  $-d[A] = k \cdot dt$
   Integration:            $$\mathbf{[A]_t = [A]_0 - k t} \quad \implies \quad \mathbf{k = \frac{[A]_0 - [A]_t}{t}}$$

                        ZERO-ORDER GRAPHICAL PLOTS
                        
         [A]_t ▲                                 Rate ▲
               │ * (y-intercept = [A]₀)               │
               │  \                                   │ ------------------- (Slope = 0)
               │   \  Slope = -k                      │
               │    \
             0 └─────*───────────► Time (t)         0 └──────────────────► [A]
conceptBreakdown.content:
A Zero-Order Reaction is one where the reaction rate is completely independent of the concentration of reactants:
$$\text{Reaction: } A \longrightarrow \text{Products} \quad \implies \quad \text{Rate} = -\frac{d[A]}{dt} = k [A]^0 = k$$

$$\mathbf{[A]_t = [A]_0 - k t \quad \implies \quad k = \frac{[A]_0 - [A]_t}{t}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 Half-Life & Completion Time for Zero-Order
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Half-Life & Completion Time for Zero-Order
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ZERO-ORDER HALF-LIFE & COMPLETION

• Half-Life (t_1/2):       t_1/2 = [A]₀ / (2k)  ⟹  t_1/2 ∝ [A]₀
• Completion Time (t_100%): t_100% = [A]₀ / k = 2 × t_1/2

Classic Examples:
1. Enzyme-catalyzed reactions at substrate saturation ([S] ≫ K_m)
2. Thermal decomposition of gases on hot metal surfaces (e.g., 2NH₃(g) ──[Hot Pt]──► N₂(g) + 3H₂(g))
3. Photochemical combination of H₂(g) and Cl₂(g) over water
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Half-Life ($t_{1/2}$)**: Time required for reactant concentration to drop to half its initial value ($[A]_{t_{1/2}} = \frac{[A]_0}{2}$):
  $$\mathbf{t_{1/2} = \frac{[A]_0}{2k} \implies t_{1/2} \propto [A]_0}$$
- **Completion Time ($t_{100\%}$)**: Time required for the reaction to reach $100\%$ completion ($[A]_t = 0$):
  $$\mathbf{t_{100\%} = \frac{[A]_0}{k} = 2 t_{1/2}}$$
- **Classic Examples of Zero-Order Kinetics**:
  1. Enzyme-catalyzed reactions at substrate saturation ($[S] \gg K_m$).
  2. Thermal decomposition of gases on hot metal surfaces (e.g., $2\text{NH}_3(g) \xrightarrow{\text{Hot Pt}} \text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g)$).
  3. Photochemical combination of $\text{H}_2(g)$ and $\text{Cl}_2(g)$ over water.

quickRevision: Enzyme saturation and NH₃ decomposition on hot Pt are zero-order.
